question.leadin: This man was born near Lake Baikal with the name Temujin ("TEH-moo-jin").
question.text: Name this man who was proclaimed "universal ruler" in a 1206 assembly.
question.clue: This creator of the Yasa law code defeated the Khwarazmian Empire with help from generals like Jebe and Subutai.

swap.text: Kazakhstan has the longest coastline on this body of water which, despite its name, is the largest lake in the world. This lake also borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan, and caviar is often procured from fish in this lake.
swap.answerHtml: Caspian Sea [or Kaspii Tenizi, or Hazar Denzi, or Hezer Denizi]
swap.clue: The world's first oil tanker sailed across this body of water from a port that produced half of the world's oil in 1900.

question.leadin: Following this man's brutal sack of Baghdad, he had human skulls stacked into giant pyramids.
question.text: Name this famously handicapped Central Asian conqueror of Mongol origin who conquered a massive empire before suddenly dying en route to an invasion of China.
question.clue: This man captured Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt at the Battle of Ankara.

swap.text: Upon their return, Marco then inherited that job, travelling along this Eurasian trade route to Chengdu and visiting Kublai in the 1270s.
swap.clue: In the plural, this term was subtitled A New History of the World in a work by Peter Frankopan, and it names Yo-Yo Ma's ensemble to promote cross-cultural artistic collaboration.

question.leadin: William Brydon was the sole survivor of a retreat made from this city to Jalalabad.
question.text: Name this city ruled by leaders such as Shah Shujah Durrani. William Elphinstone's forces were massacred while retreating from this city in 1842.
question.clue: Leaving from Khanadar, this city was captured by Ahmad Shah Durrani whose son Timur Shah moved the capital of their empire to this city in 1772.

swap.text: The heqin policy was later revived by the Tang when Princess Wencheng ("win-chung") was sent to marry this region's king Songtsen Gampo. A monastery in this Himalayan region's capital of Lhasa was built to house a Buddha statue she supposedly brought.
swap.answerHtml: Tibet [or Bod or Xizang; accept Tibetan Empire or Tufan or Tubo]
swap.clue: Tenzin Gyatso was forced to flee this region when it was conquered by the People's Liberation Army.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the tribe known as the Alans, who migrated to Europe in the late 4th and early 5th centuries.
question.text: In the late 9th century, the Alans established an independent kingdom in this mountain range. A nation in this range is often recognized as the first to establish Christianity as its official religion, doing so in 301 A.D.
question.clue: Bagrationi Dynasty rulers such as Tamar the Great led a kingdom based in this range.The Circassians were based in this range, near the site of a genocide that remains ignored underArticle 301 today.

swap.leadin: The 1881 Battle of Geok Tepe completed the Russian defeat of the people for which this nation is named.
swap.text: Name this Central Asian country with a capital at Ashgabat. It is one of the largest producers of natural gas in the world, and large parts of it are covered by the Black Sand Desert.
swap.clue: The Rukhnama, or "Book of Soul," was a propaganda work written by a former head of this state, Saparmurat Niyazov.

question.leadin: In 1839, the British deposed the king of this territory and replaced him with a puppet ruler.
question.text: Identify this modern-day country that ceded territory via the Treaty of Gandamak to British. Britain initially got involved in this country after an attack on its city of Herat.
question.clue: The Peshawar Accords ended this country's civil war, marking a victory for the Mujahideens.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
swap.text: Primarily made up of three groups the Uzbeks, the Hazara, and the Tajiks, members of this military and political organization aided in overthrowing the Taliban and found key positions in Hamid Karzai's government.
swap.answerHtml: The Northern Alliance [or The United Front for the Salvation of Afghanistan; or the UIF]

question.text: Islamist forces countering the Soviets were known by this term, which can refer to Muslim guerilla fighters.
question.clue: A manual titled for the "victory" of people known by this word prescribed 200 men to fill each "cushoon" operating rocket artillery in Tipu Sultan's Mysorean army.

swap.leadin: After being defeated by the First Turkic Khaganate and the Sasanian Empire, some rulers of these people ruled parts of Tokharistan.
swap.text: Name these people called Ye-Ta by the Chinese Wei Dynasty. Song Yun described how Buddhists were massacred by a leader of these Central Asian people not to be confused with a similarly name "Alchon" group.

question.leadin: A vizier of an empire whose capital was this city may have been a secret Manichaean.
question.text: Name this city, the capital of the Samanid Empire whose rulers commissioned Ferdowsi to write the Shahnameh. Alongside the Khanate of Khiva, an emirate ruled from this city later became a Russian protectorate.
question.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

swap.text: The Ballad of Mulan instead depicts her fighting the Rouran ("roh-rahn"), who are the first historical people of note to use this title for their rulers. This Turkic title was also given to the leader of the Mongols.
swap.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

question.text: Once the Red Army toppled Ungern von Sternberg, this early Mongolian leader liquidated Mongolian Buddhist institutions and clergy after pushing out Peljidiin Genden, who had denied Stalin's requests to do so.
question.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

swap.text: Name this republic, the last to leave the USSR. Gorbachev's replacement of Dinmukhamed Kunaev with the ethnic Russian Gennady Kolbin provoked the Jeltoqsan protests.

question.text: The Gokturks were led by this tribe and ruling dynasty. This tribe had been subjugated by the Rouran in 460, but conquered them in 552 under the leadership of Bumin Qaghan.

swap.text: The Eastern Turkic Khaganate was formed from this group who were led by the Ashina clan and formed a namesake Khaganate after succeeding the Rouran ("ROH-ran").
swap.answerHtml: Göktürks [or Blue Turks or Celestial Turks or Tūjué; accept Göktürk Khaganate]

question.leadin: They conquered their namesake city after Alp Tigin was dismissed from office and used his slaves to take it over.
question.text: Identify this Islamic dynasty based out of Afghanistan that brought Islam to the heart of India under their greatest ruler Mahmud.
question.clue: One of the dynasties that sprung up in Transoxiana after the demise of the Abbasids was this one, whose founder Sabuktigin founded it by seizing Samanid territory. Its sultan Mahmud patronized the poet Ferdowsi.

swap.leadin: A legend describes how after a stable keeper severed the cord connecting a king of this empire to heaven, the king's supporters sent a pack of dogs covered in poison to kill him.
swap.text: Name this empire ruled by Songstan Gampo and Ralpacan which collapsed in the 840s, leading to the Era of Fragmentation.
swap.clue: Ralpacan was one of this empire's Three Dharma Kings.
